title: UNDERSTANDING INFECTION: HOW GERMS MAKE YOU SICK
nextLesson: HOW DO VACCINES TRAIN YOUR BODY?

o: A pain caused by tired muscles
Harmful germs getting inside the body and multiplying
A cold feeling in the weather
questions.good: Correct! An infection is germs that get in and multiply.
questions.hint: Think about what germs do once they are inside.
questions.review: An infection is harmful germs that get inside the body and multiply.

questions.q: Which of these is a kind of germ?
questions.good: Yes! Bacteria, viruses, and fungi are the main kinds of germs.
questions.hint: Remember the three kinds shown in the second scene.
questions.review: The main germs are bacteria, viruses, and fungi.

questions.q: What is the body's first shield against germs?
questions.good: Great! Unbroken skin blocks most germs.
questions.hint: It covers your whole body on the outside.
questions.review: Unbroken skin is the first shield. A cut opens a door for germs.

questions.q: Which cells rush in to fight germs?
questions.good: Right! White blood cells attack and destroy germs.
questions.hint: They are part of your immune system.
questions.review: White blood cells surround and destroy germs.

o: Washing hands with soap and water for twenty seconds
Rinsing hands quickly with no soap
questions.q: What is the best simple habit to stop most germs?
questions.good: Excellent! Twenty seconds of soap and water removes most germs.
questions.hint: Think about the habit from the prevention scene.
questions.review: Wash with soap and water for twenty seconds.

announcements.text: Wash your hands the right way today: soap, water, and twenty full seconds.
